headline: San Francisco is the capital of the AI agent revolution—build a venture from the epicenter before the window closes.
why_now: GitHub activity for agentic workflows sits at 96 with 94% growth, signaling that the developer community is shipping tools at record speed. Hugging Face activity (92) and strong news momentum (88) confirm that enterprises are actively exploring agent deployment, creating immediate demand for founders who can package this into productized offerings. With your enterprise background and SF proximity, you are unusually well-positioned to convert this signal into a funded company in the next 12 months.
study: Week 1-2: Build deep fluency in agent orchestration—read the LangGraph and CrewAI docs end-to-end, then reimplement their quickstarts from scratch.
Week 2-3: Study Anthropic's tool-use protocol and OpenAI's function-calling specs; replicate a multi-step agent that calls a real API (e.g., Stripe or Salesforce) and handles failures.
Week 3-4: Ship two open-source micro-projects on GitHub—an eval harness for agent reliability and a reusable tool-calling wrapper—to generate signal and recruit collaborators.
Week 4-6: Interview 15 SF enterprise buyers (RevOps, IT, data leaders) about which agent workflows they would pay for; synthesize the pain points into a sharp opportunity map.
Week 6-8: Write a 4-page internal memo on your target wedge, pricing, and defensibility—treat it as the seed deck outline.

build.title: AgentOps Control Plane for Enterprise Workflow Automation
build.description: A multi-agent platform that lets enterprises deploy, monitor, and audit AI agents that execute real business workflows (e.g., contract review, lead enrichment, ticket triage) across SaaS tools. It impresses because it tackles the three things enterprises actually need—observability, permissions, and ROI measurement—which most agent demos ignore.
deliverables: Public GitHub repo with MIT license and a working end-to-end demo
Live hosted demo on Vercel with a recorded Loom walkthrough
Technical write-up on your blog or Substack showing the architecture and one real enterprise case study

publish: Post the GitHub repo on Hacker News with a thoughtful 'Show HN' title and a comment explaining the enterprise problem you solved.
Share the demo on X and LinkedIn tagging relevant SF agent communities (LangChain, CrewAI, Y Combinator AI folks); aim for 3-thread discussion, not one-off posts.
Submit a 5-minute talk proposal to the next SF AI meetup (e.g., AI Tinkerers, SF AI Tech Meetup) to build local credibility.
DM 10 SF-based technical founders and enterprise PMs with a personalized 2-sentence ask for feedback—convert two into design partners and one into a pilot.
skills: Sales and customer discovery with enterprise buyers
Defensible product thinking around AI infrastructure
risks: The agent framework landscape is shifting monthly—building too tightly to one library (LangGraph, CrewAI, Autogen) can leave you with rewrite debt within six months.
Enterprise pilots often stall at security and procurement review, so budget at least 2-3 months longer than your optimistic timeline for a first paid contract.
Agent reliability and hallucination remain unsolved for high-stakes workflows; positioning purely on autonomy rather than human-in-the-loop control can erode trust quickly.
confidence: High—the signals (96 project potential, 95 career value, 84 community activity) align tightly with your enterprise profile and SF location, and the wedge is concrete enough to test within 30 days.
